title: Multi-Agent Security Tax: Trading Off Security and Collaboration Capabilities in Multi-Agent Systems

live_model.evidence: "without defense, most models maintained high unusual but harmless instruction success rates (91-92%), with gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 being the exception at 64.4%."; results table row "gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 64.4%+-7pp ...".

prompt.location: Appendix (vaccine/system-prompt text, harmless-instruction list, and 'infection' instructions, all repeatedly referenced as "see the Appendix")
prompt.note: Judge (undated "GPT-4 Omni") resolved to gpt-4o-2024-05-13 under the pre-2024-10-02 rule, consistent with the AAAI 2025 submission timeline.

claim.metric: agent acceptance rate on harmless-but-unusual instructions, no-defense baseline
claim.location: Results table, row gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, no-defense column

data.source: Authors' own 6 harmless-but-unusual instructions and vaccine/defense prompts, printed in the Appendix

notes: 5,400 total trials span 6 agent models x 5 defense conditions x 6 instructions; n_items=180 is derived (5400/30) and is consistent with the reported +-7pp confidence interval via a binomial approximation. A separate experiment on adversarial 'infection spread' (Sec. 3.1) is distinct from this harmless-instruction helpfulness measure.
